sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Temporal Association with GLP-1 Agonists
sections.description: This section details the patient's demographic profile, medical history, and the specific chronology of symptom onset relative to semaglutide administration. It establishes the clinical picture of progressive proximal weakness and bulbar involvement while highlighting the unique timeline that distinguishes this case from acute toxic myopathy.
subtopics: Patient demographics and relevant comorbidities (obesity, NAFLD, hypothyroidism)
Chronology of events: From initial semaglutide dose to acute hospitalization and subsequent decline
Characterization of neuromuscular symptoms: Proximal weakness, dysphagia, and dysphonia
Differentiating early adverse effects (GI toxicity, AKI) from delayed autoimmune sequelae
Significance of the absence of statin exposure or other known IMNM triggers

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Workup: Laboratory, Imaging, and Histopathological Findings
sections.description: This section provides a systematic analysis of the diagnostic investigations performed. It interprets laboratory trends (CK, transaminases), advanced imaging results, and critically evaluates the muscle biopsy findings that confirm the diagnosis of Immune-Mediated Necrotising Myopathy (IMNM) despite seronegativity.
subtopics: Interpretation of Creatine Kinase (CK) trajectory: Modest initial elevation vs. massive delayed spike
Disentangling hepatic vs. muscular sources of transaminase elevation in the context of NAFLD
Autoimmune serology panel: Significance of negative HMGCR/SRP and isolated low-titer SS-B
Radiologic evidence: MRI findings of muscle edema and cardiac MRI assessment for concomitant myocarditis
Histopathological hallmarks: Necrotic fibers, macrophage infiltration (CD68+), MAC deposition, and paucity of lymphocytes

sections.description: This section explores the logical framework used to rule out alternative diagnoses and establish the link between semaglutide and IMNM. It contrasts drug-induced rhabdomyolysis with autoimmune myopathy and applies causality criteria to evaluate the likelihood of the association.
subtopics: Distinguishing Immune-Mediated Necrotising Myopathy (IMNM) from direct toxic rhabdomyolysis
Evaluation of other etiologies: Statin-negative necrotizing myopathy, viral myositis, and connective tissue diseases
Addressing the challenge of seronegative IMNM (absence of anti-HMGCR/anti-SRP)
Application of WHO-Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC) causality criteria to the case
Reasoning against a 'smoldering' pre-existing autoimmune condition based on clinical timeline

sections.description: This section outlines the multimodal treatment strategy employed, focusing on the rationale for combining high-dose corticosteroids with Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG). It tracks the patient's response to therapy, weaning protocols, and long-term functional recovery.
subtopics: Indications for aggressive upfront immunosuppression in severe bulbar/proximal weakness
Protocol for pulse steroids followed by oral tapering strategies
Role and dosing rationale for IVIG as adjunctive therapy in refractory or severe cases
Monitoring therapeutic response: Normalization of CK and resolution of MRI abnormalities
Long-term outcomes: Functional recovery, successful withdrawal of immunosuppression, and avoidance of relapse

sections.section_title: Pathophysiological Insights and Clinical Implications for GLP-1 Agonist Use
sections.description: This final section synthesizes the case findings to discuss broader clinical lessons. It reviews current knowledge regarding GLP-1 agonist-associated muscle pathology, hypothesizes potential mechanisms for immune activation, and provides guidance for pharmacovigilance in an era of expanding GLP-1 usage.
subtopics: Review of emerging literature on GLP-1 agonists and skeletal muscle adverse events
-Hypothesized mechanisms: Direct toxicity vs. immune system modulation triggering autoimmunity
-Comparison with established drug-induced IMNM entities (e.g., statin-associated)
-Clinical pearls for recognizing delayed-onset myopathy after GLP-1 initiation
-Guidelines for monitoring CK levels and managing suspected cases in clinical practice
